reviewerRole: Independent visual critic; no source or scene authoring
scope: Repair source renders and supporting geometry/UV records only; not native acceptance

masonry.verdict: Proceed to controlled native review; the widespread triangular face failure is absent in this source view, with local dark seams still requiring investigation.
improvements: Exposed areas now read as continuous stone courses and mortar behind the plaster. They no longer show the dense triangular mosaic that rejected the previous native iteration.
Thin plaster breaks and connected cracks provide a coherent layered construction cue. The geometry and UV records support a targeted repair rather than merely concealing the defect.
remainingRisks: Several outer layer ends have long black slots or dashed black gaps. The isolated presentation may expose edges normally covered by adjacent architectural trim, but assembled native views must prove that; do not treat them as automatically harmless.

A small black diamond-like notch appears near the upper middle of the right foreground panel, where a diagonal crack meets an exposed course below the gable. This is away from the far outer end. Check whether it is valid recess shadow or an unintended opening/normal discontinuity in the assembled scene.

The surviving plaster remains very even and clean, and the stone courses are regular. The source repair addresses topology, while mineral variation, localized wear and the reference's richer surface transitions still require native art review.

thresholds.verdict: Proceed to controlled native review; the reported stretched-side mapping defect is not visible in these corrected source views.
improvements: Vertical risers now show stone grain and fracture structure at a plausible scale rather than horizontal wood-like streaks.
Top slabs no longer display the conspicuous identical crack patch aligned across adjacent stones seen in the previous native close-up.
Edge chips and stone thickness remain readable, without conspicuous new holes or severe shading breaks in these two source angles.
remainingRisks: The source light is comparatively even. Correct native smoothness packing and mip/normal interpretation must be verified under the actual sun; these images cannot prove that the earlier bright edge sparkles are gone in motion.

The landing remains a regular set of similar slabs with small detached chips. Final acceptance depends on grounded assembly, controlled variation, dust in joints and the player-height reference comparison.
The distant rear foundation strip in the Field Supply source view uses a different stone pattern. Confirm that only appropriate exposed faces retain that treatment after the building is assembled.
